jobs.title: Platform Engineer - E3
jobs.description_text:
Instawork is on a mission to create meaningful economic opportunities for skilled hourly professionals in communities around the globe. Our AI-powered labor marketplace helps local businesses scale, and enables global technology companies to push the frontiers of robotics and AI. Backed by world-class investors like Benchmark, Spark Capital, Craft Ventures, Greylock, Y Combinator, and others, we’re looking for exceptional talent to reimagine the way the world works.

About IRL (Instawork Robotics Labs)

Researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a “100,000-year data gap”—the gulf between what trained AI language models and what physical robots actually have to learn from. Closing that gap is the defining infrastructure challenge of the physical AI era. IRL is Instawork’s answer to it. We deploy skilled workers into real commercial and residential environments—kitchens, warehouses, hotel floors, and homes—to capture the high-fidelity task data that the world’s leading robotics labs use to train their foundation models.

About the Role

Instawork Robotics creates the highest-quality, highest-diversity datasets for robotics and physical AI. We work with leading robotics builders and research labs to solve one of the most important challenges in robotics: closing the data gap.
As a Platform Engineer, you will build the products, services, tools, and infrastructure that power IRL’s data

Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

About this Role:

Produce high-fidelity annotations on imagery and video used to train and evaluate machine learning models. Annotators work to a defined ontology and labeling specification, meet project quality and throughput targets, and operate inside the designated annotation environment for each program. Assignments rotate across projects, modalities, and customers as program needs change.

jobs.description_text:
About the position

Our goal is to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. As an intern, you'll be paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on real-world projects we actually need done.

We’re looking for passionate and inquisitive students interested in security and technology to join us in our Hong Kong office for a Cybersecurity internship. Our Cybersecurity Engineers are responsible for being on the front lines of guarding the firm from cyber threats through investigations and incident response, as well as building tools and automation to streamline, automate, and enhance workflows, and grow our capabilities.

Our Cybersecurity team is a skilled group of programmers and security experts who are dedicated to keeping the firm safe. We consider ourselves to be tapped into developments in the broader cybersecurity space, and we can tell the difference between the latest cool hack by security researchers and what actually matters in our day-to-day work. 

While wearing the hat of an investigator, you’ll be investigating alerts, digging through activity chains, and hunting and responding to evil. You’ll gain an understanding of a wide variety of log sources, systems, and tooling, primarily in-house developed or open source.

jobs.title: Cybersecurity Engineer: Security Operations Center (SOC)
jobs.description_text:
About the position

We're looking to add a passionate Cybersecurity Engineer to our Hong Kong office to help protect Jane Street’s employees, data, and infrastructure from the wilds of the internet. Our Cybersecurity Engineers are responsible for developing and using monitoring tools to guard the firm, as well as handling incident response and remediation when a threat is found.

Our Cybersecurity team is a skilled group of programmers and security experts who are dedicated to keeping the firm safe. We consider ourselves to be tapped into developments in the broader cybersecurity space, and can tell the difference between the latest cool hack by security researchers and what actually matters in our day-to-day. In this role, you’ll carefully consider the context of our decisions as we think about the tradeoffs we’re making in our approach to resolving cybersecurity issues. We’ll expect you to apply a methodical approach to performing unstructured investigations to locate and repair the source of a security issue.

You will also act as an ambassador of best practices to the rest of the firm. Team members understand and practice good personal cybersecurity hygiene, and are able to talk to others about it. A key component of doing well in this position is bringing everyone else along with you on the cybersecurity journey, and you should be excited to learn from your colleagues and pass that learning on to new analysts.

jobs.title: Data Center Operations Engineer
jobs.description_text:
About the Position

We are looking for an experienced Data Center Operations Engineer to join a highly technical group responsible for operating and maintaining our rapidly scaling data center infrastructure. 

This is a hands-on role supporting live, mission-critical facilities while additional data halls and buildings are constructed and commissioned on the same campus. This is a role based at our mission-critical data center campus in Chicago. You will support the live portions of the campus, helping us keep live infrastructure operating reliably while bringing new capacity safely into service.

Our team is collaborative in nature, spanning many internal departments and external vendors, contractors, consultants, and operations teams. Your work will cover all aspects of our complex data center environments, including working with advanced power and cooling systems. 

Additional responsibilities of the role will include: 

  • Operating and maintaining live data center environments, including regular equipment inspections, alarm response, incident response, and follow-up
  • Troubleshooting cooling, power, controls, and monitoring issues at the cabinet, pod, and facility levels
  • Supporting and maintaining CDUs, RDHx units, and direct liquid cooling infrastructure, including hands-on tasks such as filter replacement, valve and hose checks, and leak response

jobs.title: Data Centre Facilities Engineer
jobs.description_text:
About the position

We are looking for an experienced Data Centre Facilities Engineer to join a highly technical group responsible for operating and maintaining the rapidly scaling infrastructure within our global data centres and colocation sites.

In this role, you will be responsible for liaising between internal teams and external data centres and colocation service providers to ensure 100% uptime across our critical facilities portfolio. You will also be involved with technical project management and the build out/fit out of our data centres and colocation sites. Having knowledge of the interdependencies of data centre functions and technologies is preferred.

We are looking for someone with a proven ability to deliver no matter the task, with a solid technical understanding of MEP components and the ability to make well-reasoned engineering decisions as they relate to operational risk. The right candidate will work well autonomously, manage their time exceptionally well and be able to make judgement calls with strong data and reasoning to back them up.

Our team is collaborative in nature, spanning many internal departments and external vendors, contractors, consultants and operations teams. Your specific work will cover all aspects of our complex distributed data centre and colocation environments.

jobs.title: Graphic Designer
jobs.description_text:
About the position

We're looking for a Graphic Designer to join our Creative Engagement team and bring visual life to the financial, technological and mathematical work happening at Jane Street. In this role, you'll help shape and care for how the firm looks across our many departments, programmes, spaces and events.

Our work is deeply intellectual, so we're hoping to find someone who loves taking abstract ideas and turning them into clear, engaging designs that celebrate the thoughtful things our colleagues are doing across the company.

The variety of work is what our designers love most: you might find yourself creating print and digital assets for recruiting materials, giving a conference booth its visual identity, bringing our puzzles and games to life, developing swag and branded packaging, shaping logos and brand systems and much more. We work collaboratively, so you'll get to be a design generalist and pitch in wherever the team needs you.

No previous finance experience is needed—just genuine curiosity and an enthusiasm for interesting design challenges. We do ask for a portfolio when you apply.

  • Have 6+ years of design experience across a range of project types and scales

jobs.description_text:

We are looking for an enthusiastic, motivated and technologically curious individual with a Windows security focus to join Jane Street's IT Security team. jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description_text:
About the Position

We're looking for Software Engineers who want to help us design and build the systems and tools that run the firm. You'll find Software Engineers in all parts of Jane Street, solving real problems in critical areas ranging from trading desks to our accounting team, as well as building foundational infrastructure, whether that means implementing network monitoring or risk models.

We are big believers in functional programming and, using OCaml, a statically -typed functional programming language, as our primary tool. More recently, Python has become a vital part of Jane Street's research and trading work, acting as the go-to language for data analysis, visualisation, and machine learning.

Beyond our own environment, we also recognise the value of open source software, leveraging it in our daily work and releasing over a million lines of our own code as open source. We're also always looking for ways to expand open source projects, and provide ongoing support to things like Mercurial, the OCaml compiler, and the OPAM package manager. That said, we're interested in talented engineers with experience in any language—most of us came in with little to no practical experience in OCaml before we joined.

If you'd like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of our newest hires.

We are seeking an Engineering Manager to lead LaunchDarkly’s Data Platform team and help shape the high-throughput data backbone behind our most important products. About the Job:

We’re looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the SDK team, the team behind LaunchDarkly’s developer experience across every platform. The team builds and maintains 35+ open-source SDKs, along with OpenFeature providers, event-streaming libraries, contract tests, release tooling, and the Relay Proxy. This is the code developers integrate directly into their applications and the primary way customers experience LaunchDarkly day-to-day.

Trillions of feature flag evaluations run through code this team ships, giving the team an unusually direct impact on how safely and confidently engineering organizations deliver software.

You’ll lead a senior, polyglot team working at the intersection of developer tooling, distributed systems, open source, and the next generation of software delivery. It’s an opportunity to shape a highly visible portfolio, influence how developers (including AI-assisted developers) integrate with LaunchDarkly, and help define what great developer infrastructure looks like at scale.

In 1851, a New York bookkeeper named George D. Lyman observed the same absurd ritual each afternoon: porters carried bags of coins and bundles of checks bank to bank down Wall Street, settling by hand, a fortune exposed to error and theft. Lyman's fix: send everything through one central office and settle the net. On October 11, 1853, in the basement of 14 Wall Street, 52 banks cleared $22.6 million in a single sitting. Money between banks had stopped being an event and became seamless infrastructure.

A century and a half later, the hard part is unchanged: moving money once is easy; making it work every time, for hundreds of thousands of businesses, across every rail, is hard. The bank account is where a company's financial life happens - payroll clears or it doesn't; a wire lands or a deal slips; the month closes clean, or someone loses a weekend to it. Mercury is building a business banking* product at a scale better than anything else in the market.

Business Banking is the heart of Mercury. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving deposit and payment growth, and owning business performance.

In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem.

Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what deserves attention, what to do next. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard.

Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance.

We are seeking a highly qualified Product Controller to work in our P&L Valuations team. You will investigate pricing and valuation differences and explain these to stakeholders.

jobs.description_text:
We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!

Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.

This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.

Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly’s operational and analytical systems.

This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data

A New Paradigm for Space Operations

Who We Are:

Space Kinetic is a dual-use space technology startup building a completely new architecture for space operations—one that brings the advantages of proliferated drone technology to space missions while reducing the ecosystem’s reliance on consumable fuel. In a world where many companies are focused on incrementally improving the status quo, we are focused on creating something entirely different—an architecture underpinned by new first principles to meet the opportunities and challenges of the third space age head-on. Our goal is to move away from one-to-one space architectures, where each satellite has one or a small number of primary payloads attached to the bus, and unlock a one-to-many system in which each satellite carries numerous payloads that can be deployed from their host spacecraft at high velocities without firing a thruster.

This is not a role for someone looking for a traditional 40-hour work week. Space Kinetic is building ambitious, first-of-its-kind technology, and that requires urgency, ownership, and a high level of commitment to changing the foundational assumptions for everything we do in space.
